name: Reactionaryism
summary: Reactionaryism seeks to restore a previous social order, usually a pre-revolutionary one of hereditary monarchy, an established church, noble rank and corporate estates, and rejects the egalitarian and democratic changes of modernity. It holds that legitimate authority rests on God, history and tradition rather than on reason, consent or popular sovereignty. A modern offshoot, neoreaction, shares the hostility to democracy and equality but favours sovereign rule on a corporate model.
scope: The mainstream profile is the classical counter-revolutionary reaction after 1789, centred on Joseph de Maistre's Considerations on France, with Bonald, French legitimists and Metternich's order. Neoreaction (Yarvin, Land) is noted where it agrees and answered only where the profile is plain; strands that diverge are low confidence. Fascist and other twentieth-century uses of the label are excluded.

keyFigures.name: Joseph de Maistre
keyFigures.role: Counter-revolutionary philosopher of throne and altar, author of Considerations on France.

keyFigures.name: Louis de Bonald
keyFigures.role: French clerical philosopher who, with Maistre, wanted the Bourbons and Church restored.

keyFigures.name: Curtis Yarvin
keyFigures.role: Coined neoreaction under the name Mencius Moldbug in 2008.

sources.title: Considerations on France (trans. Richard A. Lebrun, 1974)
sources.author: Joseph de Maistre
sources.usedFor: Constitutions as God's work not human design, providence, sovereignty, hereditary monarchy, Louis XVIII's restoration program.

sources.title: Reactionary
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, restoration of past order, hierarchy and authority, Church and monarchy, Metternich, legitimists.

sources.title: Joseph de Maistre
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Monarchy as divine institution, papal authority, critique of reason and Revolution, stratification, punishment.

sources.title: Neoreactionary movement
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Neoreaction on monarchy or CEO rule, exit, anti-egalitarianism, human biodiversity, the Cathedral.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pre-modern reaction looked to Church and charity for the sick; a tax-funded universal guarantee is a modern-state project the sources never tie to reactionaries.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors are not addressed by classical reaction; its stress on hierarchy and distrust of reforming legislation suggests opposition.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Classical reactionaries idealised feudal and corporate order over commerce, while neoreaction favours competing capitalist city-states, so the label gives a mixed and weak signal.

public-ownership.rationale: Not a reactionary program item; ownership by an ancien-regime crown, Church and corporate bodies is the traditional model but nationalising industry is a modern idea they would not champion.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Reactionaries defend inherited privilege and rank, so soaking the wealthy runs against them, though the sources give no tax position.

unions-good.rationale: Reaction defends the pre-revolutionary corporate order but opposes the reforming and levelling movements of modern society; independent labor unions are a post-revolution development.

property-fundamental.rationale: Restoring the old order meant restoring the property and privileges of throne, altar and nobility, but reactionaries rank property below legitimacy and tradition.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Reaction wanted guild-like corporate bodies under authority yet distrusts modern regulatory states, and neoreaction wants corporate sovereignty; no clear line.

cut-welfare.rationale: Reaction wants relief through Church and charity rather than the modern state, but the sources give no stated welfare policy.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is a socialist idea at odds with hierarchy and rank, though not discussed by reactionary sources.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Reactionaries favour strong authority and order over individual liberties; surveillance itself is an anachronistic question.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Reaction values discipline and moral order over personal license, an inference from its general stance rather than a stated position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Reactionary writers prize authority but dislike liberal rights-talk and legal egalitarianism; neoreaction explicitly opposes speech codes as Cathedral enforcement.

strong-leader.rationale: Reactionaries favour concentrated sovereign authority, from Bourbon absolutism to Yarvin's national CEO or monarch free of parliamentary gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Maistre and other reactionaries hold that sovereign authority and order are indispensable; anarchism is the opposite pole of their thought.

limit-guns.rationale: No reactionary source treats gun control; the question is modern and adherents would split between order and distrust of the state.

empower-police-military.rationale: Twentieth-century reaction is associated with restoring discipline, hierarchy and respect for authority, which includes a strong military and police.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Reactionaries uphold traditional morals, religious discipline and hierarchy against permissive social change.

decide-locally.rationale: Legitimists and corporate-order reactionaries valued old local privileges, but they also centralised sovereignty in the crown; the sources show no clear answer.

rehabilitation.rationale: Maistre defended harsh punishment and the executioner as the keystone of social order, favouring retribution over a rehabilitative approach.

traditional-family.rationale: Defence of traditional social order and inherited institutions, including the patriarchal family, is central to reactionary thought and to Maistre's counter-revolutionary program.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Reactionaries oppose such social transformations; neoreactionary writers list gay marriage among the Cathedral's agendas.

abortion-legal.rationale: Catholic throne-and-altar reaction rests on religious moral authority, which opposes legal abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Reactionaries wanted the Church re-established as state religion and blamed rationalist rejection of Christianity for the Revolution.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Reaction opposes egalitarian transformation of society, and neoreactionaries reject the premise outright.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Reactionaries hold that sex roles reflect a natural and traditional order; neoreaction rejects what it sees as Cathedral dogma.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Reaction exalts inherited institutions and traditions of the nation, idealising the national past as the basis of order.

gradual-change.rationale: Maistre said constitutions grow over time under providence rather than being built by reason, so respect for established institutions is core, though reactionaries want restoration, not just slow reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not discussed by classical reactionaries; neoreaction and later nationalist reaction lean restrictionist, an inference from their stress on cohesion.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Neoreaction and classical reaction both reject transnational liberal bodies as vehicles of progressivism, though the Pope held a universal religious authority for Maistre.

free-trade.rationale: Classical reaction was anti-commerce while neoreaction admires market-based authoritarian city-states; no uniform view.

nation-first.rationale: Reaction idealises the national past and rejects cosmopolitan liberalism, but nothing in the sources states a foreign-policy rule.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Rights-driven intervention is a liberal-universalist project reactionaries distrust, but the sources do not address it.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders embodies the universalist egalitarianism that reactionaries reject.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental degrowth is a modern concern; reactionary romanticism of the pre-industrial era gives only a weak inference.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Drastic state action driven by progressive consensus is something reactionaries distrust, an inference not found in sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Neoreactionaries embrace technology and Land links it to accelerationism, while traditionalist reactionaries see modernity as decline.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by reaction and the strands diverge.

revolution-justified.rationale: For Maistre the French Revolution was a rupture and a divine punishment, a satanic act; reaction is defined by counter-revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Maistre rejected popular sovereignty and neoreaction favours rule by competent elites over the electorate.

central-planning.rationale: Not a reactionary doctrine and incompatible with organic tradition, but not directly discussed in the sources.

socialized-markets.rationale: A socialist idea that reactionaries would oppose, though not discussed.

land-value-tax.rationale: No reactionary position known; a Georgist idea.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inherited rank and wealth are central to the hierarchy that reactionaries defend.

basic-income.rationale: A modern welfare program not found in reactionary sources; inferred from hierarchy and charity-based ideals.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Mercantilist old regimes used tariffs but neoreactionaries admire open city-states; no clear line.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Sources do not give a stable reactionary line; cameralist rulers directed economies while neoreaction favours corporate-style competition.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed; throne-and-altar reaction defended large landed estates and corporate privileges yet also peasant tradition.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money and wages is a radical utopian transformation reactionaries oppose.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Some neoreactionaries are hostile to central banks but classical reactionaries never addressed it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Reactionaries idealised guild-like corporate bodies of the old order, but the specific state-recognised bargaining model is inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Reactionaries favour monarchy or sovereign rule over ideological parties, though authoritarian in character.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Maistre held monarchy divinely sanctioned and the only stable government, and legitimists backed the Bourbon heirs.

democracy-best.rationale: Maistre ridiculed popular sovereignty and neoreactionaries call democracy degenerate and incompatible with freedom.

direct-votes.rationale: Rule by popular votes is the opposite of the reactionary premise that legitimacy rests on non-rational authority, not majorities.

workers-councils.rationale: A radical egalitarian form of rule that reactionaries oppose in favour of hierarchy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Neoreaction favours exit and small competing polities while legitimist reaction defended the integrity of the crown.

natural-rulers.rationale: Maistre supported social stratification and rule by those whom providence and tradition set above others.

political-violence-never.rationale: Maistre defended executions and the sacred role of blood in his theodicy and saw counter-revolution as legitimate, so never is rejected.

war-builds-character.rationale: Maistre described war as divine, an instrument through which providence acts on nations.

separate-church-state.rationale: Reactionaries wanted the Church reinstated as established religion and Metternich treated the Church as his main ally.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Maistre grounded law and constitutions in God, not human reason, though not necessarily in literal scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Neoreactionary patchwork and gov-corp ideas lean this way while classical reactionaries held justice a royal prerogative.

military-superiority.rationale: Order and authority are reactionary values but the sources give no explicit foreign-policy claim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not documented for classical reaction, which was dynastic and religious rather than ethnic; neoreactionary writers lean toward ethnic cohesion.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Reactionaries see society as organic hierarchy and reject class conflict as a historical driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Reactionary thought is anti-egalitarian by definition and neoreaction calls equality degenerate.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed by reactionary sources; opposes the egalitarian remedial politics usually behind it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reaction opposes progressive redress claims and is hostile to the moral framework behind them.

civilizational-union.rationale: Classical reactionaries valued Christendom as a shared order but no program for political union is documented.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Reaction places duty, loyalty and religious order above individual self-interest as a moral foundation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Maistre rejected Enlightenment rights-talk and the idea that man is born free, putting obligation to the community and its authority first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not a reactionary question; romantic traditionalists may sympathise but nothing is documented.

limit-population.rationale: Pre-modern traditionalism and religious morals incline against population control, though the sources are silent.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Reaction idealised the pre-industrial, feudal era, but it is not a stated tenet for most strands.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Neoreaction under Land embraces acceleration; traditionalist reaction opposes disruption of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Neoreactionary transhumanist sympathies conflict with religious traditionalists' views.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Neoreaction favours human sovereign CEO rule, and traditionalists reject rule by technique; no stated position.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed by classical reaction; some neoreactionaries are cryptography enthusiasts, others favour strong state power.

restore-past-order.rationale: Reactionism is defined as favouring restoration of a previous state of society they believe had positive traits missing today.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Reactionaries claim principles of tradition and legitimacy are prior to results, but neoreaction speaks of governance performance.

direct-action.rationale: Reactionaries favour restoring authority through established powers, not street-level direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: A question of anarchist method that reactionary sources do not address.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Reactionaries idealise a past hierarchical civilization such as feudal Europe, not a primitive condition.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The idea denies the hierarchy and functional ranks that reaction defends.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist principle opposed to inherited rank and privilege.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist economic principle that reactionary sources do not take up.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxian claim that reactionaries reject in defence of existing property and hierarchy.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Reaction defends aristocratic and monarchical authority, the opposite of working-class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Reaction defends traditional landholding and the old rural order.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis; reaction does not address it and its hostility is inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Libertarian-leaning neoreactionaries might agree but the monarchist tradition accepted royal taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: The harm principle is liberal individualism; reactionaries hold that authority may enforce religious and moral order.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Maistre mocked the abstract rights of man and defended corporate and hierarchical bodies over individuals as sovereign units.

conscription.rationale: Strong authority and martial order favour it, but no source states a position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Neoreactionary writers such as Land and Yarvin explicitly prefer exit to voice; classical reactionaries did not discuss it.

state-as-business.rationale: Yarvin's neocameralism and gov-corp proposals have states run as joint-stock companies whose customers can leave.

media-academia-power.rationale: Neoreactionary writers call universities and press the Cathedral, the real seat of power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Neoreactionaries endorse human biodiversity and hereditarian claims about racial differences in ability.

organic-representation.rationale: Reactionaries wanted the three Estates and corporate bodies restored as the traditional form of representation.

total-state.rationale: Reactionaries defend limited organic authority of crown, church and estates rather than total direction of society.

national-rebirth.rationale: Reaction speaks of restoration rather than radical rebirth, whereas fascist-style reaction speaks of rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not a defining reactionary stance; dynasts expanded but legitimists emphasised order.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The reactionary idealisation of feudalism favours rule resting on personal loyalty and oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Reactionaries idealised feudal order but modern adherents do not state serfdom as policy.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Neoreaction's Cathedral thesis resembles the claim, but nothing in the sources states the broader epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Maistre rejected reason as a basis for politics but affirmed divine moral order; the statement links truths to reason, which splits it.

single-common-good.rationale: Maistre distrusted rationally derived politics, preferring tradition and providence, yet affirms order as the one good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Reactionary sources give no position and strands differ.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist project the classical reactionary sources never take up, and their dynastic, religious focus gives no lean.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of firms conflicts with hierarchy and authority.

school-vouchers.rationale: Reaction wanted Church-controlled education, which vouchers could serve, but this is an inference only.

economic-freedom.rationale: Neoreaction pairs economic freedom with authoritarian rule while classical reaction ignores the claim.

rule-by-example.rationale: Maistre and legitimists stressed the moral prestige of the sovereign and reverence for authority, in addition to law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Reactionaries preferred dynastic legitimacy to the nationalist principle of self-determination, as Metternich's system did.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN postdates classical reaction, and neoreaction's distrust of international bodies is offset by no stated rule on using force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Maistre argued that human reason is disruptive and that legitimacy must rest on non-rational, religious grounds.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Preferring members of the national community is an inference; reaction does not address welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Discipline and work ethic fit the reactionary temperament, but it is not stated.

class-collaboration.rationale: Reactionaries view society as an organic hierarchy in which orders cooperate rather than fight.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Reaction values inherited cultural and religious institutions above reform.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts of dominated states are an anti-imperialist idea that reactionary writers do not discuss.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organise nationally is a socialist-internationalist debate the reactionary sources do not enter.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Reactionaries uphold traditional sex roles, and neoreactionaries decry the destruction of traditional sexual norms.

ban-interest.rationale: Medieval church doctrine banned usury but modern reactionaries do not press the point.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Neoreactionary figures hold race-realist views but no consistent legal segregationism is documented.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist view that reactionaries reject, seeing the state as sacred order.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy lies outside both Maistre's counter-revolution and neoreaction's governance writing, so no position follows.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Insistence on shared culture follows from reactionary traditionalism, though not documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: The Great Replacement theory belongs to the wider far right; classical reactionaries did not hold it and neoreaction is mixed.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary representation itself is distrusted by reactionaries, so electoral rules matter little to them.

national-mission.rationale: A mission to spread one's government abroad is not a reactionary theme, since restoration looks inward to the national past.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Reaction regards hierarchy between the sexes as natural and legitimate, not as a structural injustice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Neoreactionaries hold that elites of the Cathedral dominate, while classical reactionaries defended elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics appears in some neoreactionary thought but not in classical reaction, which was religious.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Reaction defends authority and its agents, an inference only.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Not a reactionary view; they want strong rather than minimal authority, but neoreaction is sometimes libertarian.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Documented for some neoreactionaries, not classical reaction.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Maistre defended stratification and rejected born-free rhetoric, and neoreactionaries reject equality outright.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist internal dispute that reactionaries do not address.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Reaction rejects the postcolonial lens though it never addressed it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Reaction defended a society of orders with differentiated legal privileges.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Catholic established-church reactionaries favoured a state religion with limited toleration, as in the Declaration of Verona.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu-nationalist demand outside the reactionary program.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Reactionaries wanted the Church re-established and Jesuit-style education defended.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Soviet doctrine reactionaries do not address.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Maistre rejected popular sovereignty and social contract theory, grounding authority in God and history.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade balance doctrine is not part of reactionary texts, and neoreactionary city-state admirers favour open commerce.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced minority removal is not stated in the classical sources and adherents would not agree on it today.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Reaction accepts state force and counter-revolutionary violence to uphold order.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Reactionaries reject the idea of progress and view struggle as reflecting providential order rather than driving improvement.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Order-minded reaction would not tolerate revolutionary parties, an inference from its opposition to revolution.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory of liberty that reactionaries would not adopt.

separated-powers.rationale: Maistre favoured a sovereign with undivided authority, though he praised mixed ancient constitutions.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist concept foreign to reaction.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Religious charity is a duty of reactionary Catholicism, but the legal priority framing is modern.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy question outside the reactionary sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Order and authority incline to restriction, an inference.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian explanation of poverty is not part of the reactionary sources I opened.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Neoreactionary writers argue diversity impairs social order, and reaction values cohesion in tradition.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Random selection contradicts hierarchy and natural rule.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Maistre and reactionaries accept strong exceptional authority to defend order.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Food price fixing was an old-regime practice, but the sources do not tie reactionaries to any price policy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Reaction favoured censorship of dangerous opinion by Church and state, but party control is a modern device.

party-commands-army.rationale: Reaction prefers the crown or head of state to command armed forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Caution on membership of the community fits reactionary traditionalism, but is unstated.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egalitarian pay rules are alien to a social order of rank.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Reaction distrusts party politics altogether, so internal party discipline is not a question it frames.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Neoreaction and legitimist traditionalism oppose supranational liberal unions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Reactionaries favour the monarch or sovereign commanding the army and appointing the government.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Reactionary Catholicism stresses hierarchical authority of bishops and the pope.

clerical-rule.rationale: Maistre gave the Pope supreme spiritual authority, but political rule by senior clerics is not a general reactionary doctrine.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist slogan opposed by reactionaries who defend their states.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Reactionaries sought religious and moral order in culture and supported censorship by church and state.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; neoreaction prefers permanent sovereign over elections anyway.

recall-officials.rationale: Popular recall expresses popular sovereignty that reactionaries reject.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed; Metternich's system relied on alliances of conservative powers but modern strands vary.

people-in-arms.rationale: The armed citizenry belongs to the revolutionary tradition; reactionaries prefer the crown's army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Reactionaries idealised the rural feudal and traditional world prior to the revolutions.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; neoreactionaries criticise universities and elites but Maistre admired the clergy.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Reaction holds its own civilisation's inherited order higher and rejects relativism.

death-penalty.rationale: Maistre defended the executioner as indispensable to social order and the blood of punishment as expiatory.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Reactionary religious traditionalists oppose such curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious establishment favours it but it is a modern controversy.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Dynastic and hereditary thinking inclines this way, an inference.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language rights for minorities are a late liberal concern not addressed by reactionary writers, and the stress on cohesion tilts mildly against.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not discussed; reaction favoured an established church, with limited toleration for others in Louis XVIII's program.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's individuality ideal is opposed by reactionary respect for custom.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt relief is a modern development issue the sources do not touch.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A postcolonial development thesis not discussed by reactionary writers.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Maistre argued that constitutions cannot be written by human assemblies and called written ones scraps of paper.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Neoreaction admires developmental authoritarian states like Singapore, but classical reaction is silent.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Reaction's emphasis on charity is personal and religious, and global aid duties are not stated.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear policy is not addressed in the reactionary sources opened.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Reaction favours hereditary headship rather than election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not a topic of classical reaction, and neoreactionary views on it are mixed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise in peace deals is not discussed in the reactionary sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic reaction accepted social duties of property, but this is a modern formulation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A dispute within the Marxist left about the Soviet economy, irrelevant to reaction's stance.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not a reactionary theme in the sources opened.

collective-defense.rationale: Collective defence alliances such as NATO are not discussed in reactionary sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International-law doctrine on annexation is not part of reactionary writing; Metternich's order did respect dynastic claims.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Reactionaries and Maistre wanted the Church independent, with the Pope above temporal sovereigns, and the Church reinstated.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A monarch above party fits the legitimist model, though reactionary monarchs governed rather than reigned.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Legitimists defended unity of the crown, but the sources do not discuss it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special regional arrangements, as in one country two systems, are not addressed by the reactionary sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Maistre treated monarchy as divinely sanctioned, though divine descent is not required.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is not discussed in the reactionary sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: Reaction holds that human nature and inherited order matter more than environment.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Maistre held sovereignty to be absolute and undivided, but modern reactionaries accept traditional constraints.

space-expansion.rationale: Not stated; neoreaction fans of space exist but most reactionaries do not address it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Maistre praised mixed ancient arrangements but stressed single sovereigns; the sources do not settle it.

leader-cult.rationale: Reactionary sacral monarchy differs from modern cult of personality.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; traditional family order inclines against it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine foreign to reaction.

land-redistribution.rationale: Taking estates from owners violates the restored property order.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not addressed in the reactionary sources opened.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims on territory by nationality are an irredentist theme absent from dynastic reaction, which tied claims to dynasty.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Catholic established-church reaction favoured state religion with limited toleration, so punishing apostasy is not stated.

women-must-cover.rationale: A different religious tradition's demand, not addressed.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed in reactionary writing, though distrust of supranational bodies hints against.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are not part of the reactionary sources, which rest on dynasty and church.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural autonomy is not a theme in the reactionary texts opened.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A question internal to minority politics, not addressed by reactionary sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Maistre saw providence and religion as drivers of history, not economic base.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust law is not discussed, and corporate bodies were part of the old order they admired.

no-bailouts.rationale: Neoreaction is sceptical of bailouts but classical reaction is silent.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Neoreaction rejects both courts and majorities as Cathedral instruments.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for parity express egalitarian transformation that reactionaries oppose.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs are not a reactionary doctrine in the sources I opened.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Standards in trade deals are a modern liberal policy absent from reactionary sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: A socialist idea not found in reactionary texts.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Reaction defends hereditary rank, privilege and the nobility against the Revolution's abolition of them.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Reaction values the national past as the foundation of order.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hierarchical thinking inclines this way but no source states it.

patriotic-education.rationale: Reaction wants loyalty and respect for authority taught.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Neoreactionaries oppose racial preferences as part of egalitarian doctrine.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed in the reactionary sources I opened.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whether capitalism escapes collapse is a Marxist debate, and reactionary sources do not take part.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not discussed in the reactionary sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency theory prescriptions are outside reactionary writing.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis about worker exploitation, not engaged by reactionary writers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Neoreactionaries favour freedom of association and scepticism of anti-discrimination law, but classical reaction is silent.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Maistre mocked written declarations of rights as products of reason rather than history.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Treaty validity after colonialism is not discussed by reactionary writers.

elective-rulers.rationale: Reactionaries favour hereditary succession against elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Not addressed; liberum veto is Polish tradition, unrelated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Maistre denied a right of subjects to depose sovereigns.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Reactionaries oppose parliamentary supremacy and want the monarch's sovereignty.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in Maistre or in the neoreactionary sources opened.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in the reactionary sources opened.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Reaction defends privilege together with traditional obligations of the elite, with the Church caring for the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Reactionaries favour active duty to the throne and altar, though exit is stressed by neoreaction.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Neoreaction has its own account of cultural elites shaping opinion, but not this Marxist framing.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is Marxist, though neoreaction's Cathedral idea is a parallel claim that elites rule through culture.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is a left framework that reactionary sources do not discuss.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving office for natives is not stated, though the stress on community membership leans mildly toward it.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist debate about national paths, not part of reactionary sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not discussed in the reactionary sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist claims after past wars are not part of the reactionary sources opened.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not discussed by reactionary writers; their opposition to egalitarian redress gives a weak lean against.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Neoreaction and traditionalist right oppose anti-fascist orthodoxy as part of progressive consensus.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The equivalence debate is not addressed by classical reaction and strands are likely to differ.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Documented only for fringe neoreactionary writers; strands differ.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Reaction values inherited symbols and tradition.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Neoreactionary writers treat gender egalitarianism as ideology, but nothing stated here.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the reactionary sources opened.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Maistre argued constitutions grow organically from a people's history and cannot be imported by reason.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Reactionary politics values discipline and the army as a guardian of order.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paying for domestic work is a feminist demand not addressed by reactionaries, whose family model points mildly against.

filial-duty.rationale: Reaction upholds hierarchy and respect for authority beginning in the family.

office-by-exam.rationale: Examination for office is not discussed; reaction favoured hereditary and appointed offices.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Strategic-industry ownership rules are not discussed in the reactionary sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic traditionalist reaction opposes easy divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates express popular sovereignty, opposite to reaction.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed by reactionary sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; feudal tenure aside, reaction defends private estates.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Louis XVIII's program kept an Estates-General that could vote taxes while retaining the king's right to dismiss it, so parliament only weakly constrains.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not part of the reactionary sources opened.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership rules are not discussed in the sources opened.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Neoreactionaries reject this egalitarian legal doctrine.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Reaction criticises materialism, but not a stated tenet.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert support of insurgents is not discussed, though Metternich's order opposed revolutionary movements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc interventions are not discussed in reactionary writing, though Metternich's order did support interventions against revolutions.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign money are not discussed; neoreaction blames the Cathedral rather than business.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Funding restrictions on NGOs are not addressed by the sources opened.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Traditional family support suggests yes, but it is unstated.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchase are not addressed by the sources opened.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee is a modern social-democratic idea that reactionary sources do not take up.

democratic-peace.rationale: Reactionaries reject democracy as best form and its peace claims.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Maistre held that obedience to established authority is a religious duty and the basis of social order.

non-intervention.rationale: Metternich's order intervened against revolutions, but a general non-intervention norm is not discussed, so the lean is weak.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union form is not a reactionary concern, and the lean reflects general distrust of labor organization.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Some reactionary writers blamed Jacobins, Masons or philosophes, but a general ethnic conspiracy thesis is not core.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Religious marriage is a keystone of traditional order.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; reaction favoured authority's discretion.

local-production.rationale: Local production is a green and distributist theme absent from reactionary sources.

informal-organisation.rationale: An anarchist form of organization opposed to hierarchy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Reaction and neoreaction distrust international legal bodies and defend sovereign authority.

religious-nation.rationale: Reaction wanted Catholicism restored as religion of state and nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary deference is a specifically East Asian question reactionary sources do not discuss.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in the reactionary sources opened.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist thought on personal property not addressed by reaction.

defeat-communism.rationale: Reaction opposes revolutionary egalitarianism and the twentieth-century right defined itself against communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery models are not discussed in the sources opened.

religion-illusion.rationale: Maistre treated religion as the foundation of social order and blamed its rejection for revolutionary chaos.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Reaction rejects the idea of progress, but neoreaction values capitalist dynamism.

socialized-care.rationale: Reaction defends the family as the unit that cares for children.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not documented as a reactionary position.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty rights of nations within states are not addressed in reactionary sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperative self-governing communities belong to anarchist and utopian traditions, which reaction rejects in spirit.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement policy to alter regional demographics is not discussed in the sources opened.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Not addressed; classical reaction rejected both modernity, neoreaction favours capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious land claims are not discussed in the sources opened, although reaction values historical tradition.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not documented as a reactionary doctrine.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditional morality and religious law support it, but modern reactionaries differ.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Order-minded authority supports suppressing revolutionary opposition, an inference.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Reactionaries sought Church re-establishment and Maistre treated religion as the state's foundation.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial economics is not discussed in the reactionary sources opened.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine outside the Christian reactionary sources.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Rebellion against irreligious rulers is a jihadist doctrine, and Maistre denied subjects' right to depose sovereigns.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Participation in rule by ordinary people contradicts hierarchy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Neoreaction rejects intersectionality as Cathedral doctrine.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Reaction sits firmly in right-wing politics and stresses its opposition to the left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation theory is Marxist and the reactionary sources do not engage it, though they criticise capitalist modernity differently.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Maistre insisted authority derives from God and that constitutions are God's work, not of the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; reactionaries favour religion's public presence.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A workplace law issue not addressed by reactionary sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mixed economy formulas are not discussed in reactionary sources.

rich-first.rationale: Hierarchy and unequal outcomes are accepted, though not stated in this form.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc neutrality is not discussed in the sources opened.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Legitimists backed the direct heirs of the Bourbon dynasty and Louis XVIII's program restored hereditary monarchy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking proposals are not discussed in the sources opened.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF conditionality is not discussed in reactionary sources.

property-franchise.rationale: The Restoration's narrow franchise reflected reactionary preference for restricted suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim opposed to the reactionary view of natural hierarchy.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept not discussed by reactionary sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist critique of press freedom not discussed by reaction.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Reaction rejects limits on sovereign but accepted customary law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Not a documented program of classical reaction.

online-participation.rationale: Mass participation conflicts with reactionary distrust of popular rule.

open-government-data.rationale: Neoreaction proposes formalist rule and some transparency, but this is not stated.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Church-established reaction favoured religious marriage, but legal limits on interfaith marriage are not documented.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts of minority businesses are not documented as reactionary doctrine.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random citizen deliberation expresses popular sovereignty that reactionaries reject.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Reaction defends inherited doctrine and Church authority against modernising reinterpretation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Reactionaries do not hold liberty as the central value and the sources do not address wealth concentration.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Opposes social transformation in traditional institutions.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Maistre held atheism and philosophism responsible for revolutionary terror.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Maistre made the executioner central to order.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational arrangements are not discussed in the reactionary sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Reaction envisions Church and community charity rather than state welfare.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits for elected officials are not a reactionary theme, since reaction favours permanent hereditary rule over elections, so the lean is weak.

vote-delegation.rationale: Expands democratic control, opposite to reactionary view.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk policy is not discussed in classical reaction; some neoreactionary circles care but not as a program.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Catholic hierarchy is male-only and reaction defends it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting rights for non-members clash with the traditional community.

rent-control.rationale: Rent regulation is not discussed in the sources opened.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property abolition is not discussed in the sources opened.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Youth movements are a fascist-era practice not discussed in the classical reactionary sources.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not discussed in the sources opened.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official recognition of genocide is not discussed in the sources opened.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Reaction defends inherited property and rank.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Maistre defended killing for justice and war.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Reactionaries idealise continuity of national tradition and the monarchy.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Maistre praised sacrifice and royalist martyrdom, though national sainthood is an inference.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Maistre cast the Revolution as a fight to the death between Christianity and philosophism and as divine punishment.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora-homeland relations are not discussed in the sources opened.

culture-before-state.rationale: The order of cultural and state renewal is not discussed in the sources opened.

god-not-male.rationale: Traditional Catholic reaction holds fixed doctrine.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist exegesis conflicts with inherited authority.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Economic nationalism by majority is not discussed in the sources opened.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Merging administrative units for one people is not discussed in the sources opened.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence from party and state is not discussed in the reactionary sources.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: An internal socialist debate that reactionary sources do not enter.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of water and local services is not discussed in the sources opened.

second-chamber.rationale: Louis XVIII's program restored the three Estates and a hierarchy of orders, and Metternich favoured existing institutions.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of production is not discussed, and reaction defends private estates.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Confederal municipalism is a libertarian-socialist model foreign to reaction.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not discussed in classical reaction; some neoreactionaries favour deregulation but not as a stated position.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Life-extension policy is not discussed in the sources opened.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened.

person-over-state.rationale: Maistre subordinated individuals to sovereign and religious order.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Maistre insisted that politics rests on religion and the spiritual order, against material rationalism.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Sovereign authority is undivided in the reactionary view, but not stated for regions.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is not discussed in the sources opened.

dense-cities.rationale: Rural idealisation gives a weak inference.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Maistre regarded war as divine and not merely defensive.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Language-based nationhood is a nationalist idea, while reaction defined community by dynasty and religion.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates are not discussed in the sources opened.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A nationalist grievance theme not found in the sources opened.

free-public-college.rationale: Higher education finance is not discussed in the sources opened.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxes are not discussed in the sources opened.

future-generations.rationale: Reaction's inherited-tradition stance includes duty to hand down the order.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Distinct sex roles imply distinct values, inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Arms control is not discussed in the sources opened.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital controls are not discussed in the sources opened.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Authority-centred reaction accepts state monopoly, an inference.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Obedience and discipline are core reactionary values.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Collective bargaining is not discussed in the sources opened.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits for low-paid families are not discussed in the sources opened.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal fiscal rules are not discussed in the sources opened.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global economic restructuring is not discussed in the sources opened.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Maistre held revolution and breaking established order a catastrophe, and reaction aims at restoration.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Neoreactionary patchwork supports competing systems but classical reaction does not.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is not discussed in the sources opened.

sacred-nation.rationale: Reaction treats the nation and its institutions as an inherited order outlasting individuals, though it is more dynastic and religious.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is not discussed in the sources opened.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation theory is not discussed in the sources opened.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Maistre argued from fixed human nature, that man is not redesigned by reason.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting is not discussed in the sources opened.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Maistre defended Catholicism as the true religion, not all faiths as equal.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm support is not discussed in the sources opened.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear policy is not discussed in the sources opened.

workers-own-party.rationale: A labor-party strategy not addressed by reaction, which distrusts party politics and class organisation.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed in the reactionary sources opened, so no lean is documented.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Traditional inheritance favoured male heirs, a weak inference.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Environmental liability law is not discussed in the sources opened.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Hereditary authorities in lawmaking fit reaction, but it is unstated.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental priority over liberty is not discussed in the sources opened.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Maistre favoured severe fixed punishment, inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Union membership rules are not discussed in the sources opened.

voter-id.rationale: Voting identification is not discussed; the lean follows reaction's wish to narrow the electorate.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Reaction favoured an established church above others.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Reaction rejects democracy, but the definition of democracy as procedure is not discussed in the sources opened.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Order-minded authority inclines yes, not stated.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is not discussed in the sources opened.

women-suffrage.rationale: Reaction opposes democratic expansion and the Restoration's narrow franchise; strands vary.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Maistre and reaction treat religion as the support of social order, and the sources record a denial of this claim only indirectly.

race-social-construct.rationale: Neoreactionaries endorse human biodiversity and reject this.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Homesteading is a libertarian property theory, not discussed in the sources opened.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Reaction and neoreaction oppose supranational legal bodies.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Maistre's Catholicism rests on Church authority and tradition more than literal scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Women's participation in Indigenous self-government is not discussed in the sources opened.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Reaction defends the old order, not Soviet-style states.

indirect-election.rationale: Reaction prefers appointment and estates to direct democracy.

national-church-status.rationale: Reactionaries sought the Church's re-establishment as the state religion and Metternich treated the Church as the main ally of order.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Territorial autonomy for minorities is not discussed in the sources opened.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Maistre ridiculed popular sovereignty, an inference to plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Postcolonial borders are not discussed in the sources opened.

simple-living.rationale: Voluntary simplicity is not discussed in the sources opened.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Settlement limits in indigenous regions are not discussed in the sources opened.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Maistre favoured formal judicial punishment and the executioner, not lawless killing.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; neoreactionaries admire Chinese-style authoritarian development but no policy stated.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Protection of co-nationals abroad is not discussed in the sources opened.

self-ownership.rationale: Libertarian-leaning neoreaction might agree, classical reaction rejects.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption tax rates are not discussed in the sources opened.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Targeting of social spending is not discussed in the sources opened.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Neoreaction favours a sovereign unmediated by party politics, inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Neoreaction attacks crony elites, but classical reaction defended privileged corporate bodies, so no line is documented.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Reaction wants religious establishment in politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Reaction pairs tradition with modern means in neoreaction, not explicitly in classical reaction.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource nationalism is not discussed in the sources opened.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language naming disputes are not discussed in the sources opened.

positive-liberty.rationale: Material-means conceptions of freedom belong to the progressive left; reaction rejects liberty-talk in general, though not discussed here.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of divided nations is not discussed in the sources opened.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: classical reaction defended inherited rank and estates rather than voluntary-exchange entitlement, while neoreaction leans proprietarian, so adherents split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from reaction's distrust of reforming legislation; the sources never discuss financial taxes.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from reaction's acceptance of natural hierarchy and neoreaction's human biodiversity theme; classical reactionaries did not address the question.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Maistre grounds authority in God and tradition and stresses obedience to sovereigns, yet divine law outranks human decrees; the sources do not settle which way adherents lean.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from reaction's stress on settled social order and distrust of modern progress; neoreaction's techno-optimists are a split minority.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from Metternich's order and the legitimist concert of independent monarchies, which preferred a balance among states to a single hegemon.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: reaction rejects the egalitarian, materialist theories of the Revolution and its heirs, though it never addresses value theory directly.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Reaction values loyalty to throne, church and nation within a hierarchy of estates, but does not frame this as service to workers, so the statement fits it only loosely.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: reaction places religion, tradition and authority above material interests, though it has no stated view on what the left should do.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from reaction's hostility to revolutionary socialism and one-party rule by a communist party.

missingStatements.text: Constitutions grow out of a people's history and cannot be designed on paper by human reason.
missingStatements.rationale: Maistre's chapter on political constitutions argues that man modifies but never creates a constitution, which is God's work.

missingStatements.text: A revolution against an established political order is a crime against divine order.
missingStatements.rationale: Maistre treats the French Revolution as satanic and a providential punishment, and reaction is defined by opposition to such rupture.

notes: Classical reaction and neoreaction differ on markets, technology and religion, so those answers are low. Many answers are low-confidence inferences because classical reactionary writers never addressed modern issues.
